entries.cause: Gall midges (Cecidomyiidae); on mango Erosomyia indica and Procontarinia mangiferae are named
symptoms: Tiny maggots tunnel inside the flower stalk and tender parts.
The flower panicle can be destroyed completely before flowering.
Flower stalks bend and dry up.
Later attacks can affect fruits and tender leaves.
entries.look_alikes: Hopper damage also dries flowers, but hoppers are visible wedge-shaped insects with honeydew and sooty mould.
cultural_actions: Collect and destroy infested panicles, leaves and twigs.
Plough the orchard to expose resting stages in soil to the sun.
entries.when_to_act: Sources say spray dimethoate at the bud burst stage.

ask_back.question: Are flower panicles bending, drying and dying before they open?
Can you see sap-sucking wedge-shaped hoppers on the panicles?

entries.cause: Bactrocera dorsalis (fruit fly); sources also name B. correctus and B. zonatus on mango
symptoms: Female pierces ripening fruit with a pointed egg-laying tube.
Eggs are laid in small groups inside the fruit pulp.
White maggots feed in the pulp.
Fruit may look normal outside but rots inside and drops.
entries.look_alikes: Mango seed weevil also spoils fruit, but its grub bores into the stone, not the soft pulp.
cultural_actions: Collect and destroy fallen and infested fruits regularly.
Plough or rake soil under trees to expose the pupae.
Hang methyl eugenol traps before fruits mature.
Harvest mature-green fruit and remove damaged fruit.

treatment_options.note: Trap lure; follow trap maker's label; no dose

treatment_options.active_ingredient: Malathion in methyl eugenol trap or in bait
Protein hydrolysate or jaggery bait spray with insecticide

entries.when_to_act: Hang traps and apply bait before fruits mature, before egg laying starts; sprays only before harvest as per label.

ask_back.question: Are there small holes or scars on ripening fruit with white maggots inside the pulp?
Is the grub inside the hard stone instead of the pulp?

entries.caveats: Written for Indian mango. Post-harvest hot water treatment is also described by sources; ask your KVK. Check label for pre-harvest waiting period.

entries.cause: Mango hoppers Idioscopus clypealis, Idioscopus niveosparsus (nitidulus in ICAR source) and Amritodus atkinsoni
symptoms: Wedge-shaped nymphs and adults crowd on flower panicles and tender shoots.
They suck sap, so flowers dry and fruit drops.
Leaves curl and wilt.
Sticky honeydew attracts black sooty mould.
entries.look_alikes: Gall midge also kills panicles, but the damage is from tiny maggots inside the flower stalk.
cultural_actions: Prune to keep the canopy open.
Avoid dense planting and control growth flushes.
Keep the orchard clean.
Protect natural enemies like lacewings, ladybirds, spiders and egg parasites.
entries.when_to_act: Spray first at early panicle emergence if hoppers are above the local threshold; later at full panicle and after fruit set.

ask_back.question: Do you see small wedge-shaped hopping insects on panicles with sticky honeydew?
Are panicles dying from tunnelling maggots inside the stalk?

entries.name_en: Mango shoot borer and stem borer
entries.cause: Shoot borer Chlumetia transversa (moth); stem borer Batocera rufomaculata (beetle)
symptoms: Shoot borer: dark pink caterpillar tunnels down the leaf midrib and into the shoot.
Tender shoots wilt, leaves drop, and shoot tips look bunchy.
Stem borer: grubs make tunnels and cavities in stems and branches.
Branches dry and may die in severe attack.
entries.look_alikes: Dieback from disease also dries shoots, but borer damage shows tunnels and excreta.
cultural_actions: Remove and destroy attacked shoots.
Do summer ploughing to expose moth pupae.
Cut and destroy affected branches with grubs.
Clean the bored holes and plug them.
Keep the orchard clean and healthy; remove dead trees.

treatment_options.active_ingredient: Dichlorvos on cotton wool in cleaned stem holes
Malathion on cotton wick in cleaned stem holes

entries.when_to_act: Shoot borer: spray when a new flush starts and repeat through the flush. Stem borer: treat holes when found.

ask_back.question: Is the shoot tunnelled and wilting from the tip downward?
Are young leaves cut or scraped at the tip, with no tunnel?

entries.cause: Sternochetus mangiferae (weevil beetle); S. frigidus not covered by opened sources
symptoms: Adults are dark brown beetles.
Female lays eggs under the skin of marble-sized fruit.
White legless grubs bore through pulp to the seed.
They feed on the seed coat and the seed inside.
Pulp may be discoloured around the damaged spot.
entries.look_alikes: Fruit fly maggots feed in the soft pulp; seed weevil grubs end up in the stone.
cultural_actions: Collect and destroy fallen infested fruits.
Plough or dig soil after harvest to expose hiding weevils.
Destroy leftover seeds.
Keep tree basins clean so adults cannot hide.
Use sticky bands on the upper trunk to block weevil movement.
entries.when_to_act: Spray at the marble stage of fruit and again after fruit set, as per label.

ask_back.question: Is there a white legless grub or tunnel inside the seed (stone)?
Are the maggots in the soft pulp, with small egg-laying holes in the skin?

entries.cause: Deporaus marginatus (weevil beetle, family Attelabidae); attacks mango and cashew
symptoms: Beetles scrape young leaf tissue and cut the leaf tip.
Female lays eggs on tender leaves and cuts them off.
Young leaves turn brown, curl and fall.
Cut leaf pieces pile up under the tree.
entries.look_alikes: Shoot borer also kills tender shoots, but borer damage is a tunnel inside the shoot.
cultural_actions: Collect fallen cut leaf pieces from the orchard floor regularly.
Plough soil under the tree crown.
Watch tender flushes closely in the rainy season.
In nurseries, net or bag young plants (as tested in one study).
entries.when_to_act: Act early when new leaves are small and tender; watch during rains and new flushes.

ask_back.question: Are young leaf tips cut or scraped, with cut pieces on the ground?
Is the young shoot tunnelled and wilting?
